$comment: Destination: ci/test-floor.json in nfc-development.
Read by scripts/ci/assert-tests-executed.mjs in the Tests job of ci.yml.
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR. jest exiting zero and jest having tested something are
different claims. In this repository they have come apart in every way they can: the
configuration failed to parse, so no test file was ever discovered; bypassing it, all
eight suites failed to compile, which jest reports as failed suites and zero tests;
and repairing the imports of those suites without reading their assertions would have
turned them green while asserting an 840 byte NTAG216 limit against a 256 byte
ST25TV02KC. minimumTests is the committed statement of how many tests must actually
execute, so that none of those states can be read as success.
THE ZERO IS DELIBERATE, DATED, AND IT EXPIRES. The eight dead suites were deleted in
PR 6 of the consolidation plan. Between that deletion and the replacement landing,
there is genuinely nothing for jest to run, and the honest way to record that is a
zero floor with an expiry rather than a passing check that means nothing. The
assertion script REFUSES a zero without an expiry, warns loudly on every run while the
window is open, and fails the build the day after it closes.
RAISE IT, DO NOT EXTEND IT. When the replacement unit tests land, set minimumTests to
the number they execute and delete expires and reason. Extending the date is a
decision about a contractual gate and belongs in the decision log, naming who asked
and what moved, not in a quiet edit to this file.
The API surface is covered separately by contract-tests/, which runs under node --test
rather than jest and asserts its own operation coverage against the OpenAPI document.
That suite has its own required status check and is not counted here.
reason: Window between deleting the eight dead suites (PR 6) and landing their replacement. Closes at the end of the M3 window, Friday 11 September 2026.
